W.note: Clean graph with live marker and stats, but its three curves are near-duplicates (same set as Z) and the sticky feel comes only from the 1.44 s hold, not the curve itself.

X.note: Its Sticky S-curve visibly lingers at both ends, Punch overshoots about 9.8 percent, and Snap-settle is a clean firm stop, but the values and graphs are small and the overshoot is clipped by the track edge.

Y.note: Grip Hold gives a genuinely sticky S-curve and the three shapes differ, but there is no graph, no measured values and no hold, so the presentation is bare.

Z.note: The best-presented page with tags, live readout and Play once under reduced motion, but its curves are near-identical and none of them really clings, and it leaves a dead placeholder function in the source.
